rules.title: Unconscionable rent increase prohibition (Anti-Eviction Act)
rules.requirement: New Jersey has no state rent control law, but a rent increase must not be unconscionable, meaning so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person. The increase must also comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenants facing a rent increase; where no municipal rent control exists, a judge decides in a nonpayment eviction action whether the increase was unconscionable.
rules.penalty: Tenant may file a complaint with a municipal rent control board where one exists; otherwise a judge decides in the landlord's eviction action whether the increase is unconscionable.
rules.quoted_span: The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.interaction_text: must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases

rules.title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law exemption from local rent control
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinances for 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.coverage_text: Newly constructed multiple dwellings, with respect to local rent control ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.interaction_text: newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building

rules.title: No rent increases to cover condominium/cooperative conversion costs
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion.
rules.coverage_text: All tenants in a building converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, regardless of whether they are eligible for protected tenancy as senior citizens or disabled persons.
rules.exemptions: Rents may still be increased to cover the cost of new services or amenities.
rules.quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

rules.title: Notice to quit and notice of rent increase before eviction for nonpayment of increased rent
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot raise rent mid-lease; to evict for nonpayment of an increased rent, the owner must first serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. The tenant may remain as long as they pay any legal increase in rent.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants subject to the Anti-Eviction Act facing a rent increase.
rules.citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f); Anti-Eviction Act, N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 et seq.
rules.quoted_span: This law provides that before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. This notice does not mean that the tenant must actually leave; the tenant has the right to remain as long as they pay any legal increase in rent.
